chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman from Mis'mam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The fat camel (al-jallalah) — its meat is not to be eaten and its milk is not to be drunk until it has been fed [on clean fodder] for forty days. And the fat cow — its meat is not to be eaten and its milk is not to be drunk until it has been fed for forty days. And the fat sheep — its meat is not to be eaten and its milk is not to be drunk until it has been fed for five days. And the fat duck — its meat is not to be eaten until it has been tied [confined] for five days. And the chicken [for] three days.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali, peace be upon him).
key_terms.تُرْبَطَ: It is tied/confined (to restrict movement and change diet).
key_terms.جَلَّالَة: An animal fed primarily on impure or unclean fodder, making its meat and milk temporarily prohibited.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of Jallalah animals and how long must they be fed clean fodder?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the specific purification periods for 'Jallalah' animals, distinguishing between ruminants and poultry based on the time required for impure fodder to be metabolized and cleared from their bodies. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on removing physical impurities (najasah) from food sources to ensure ritual purity, a concept deeply rooted in the practices of the Imams. The detailed differentiation highlights the scholarly attention to biological processes in determining halal status.
